title: Normalize ledger to cent-resolution and deterministic export tiling to eliminate fractional-line drift
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We are seeing persistent micro-deltas (±1 cent) in Stripe invoice exports for a subset of customers with mixed-currency billing, reserved-capacity discounts, and mid-hour quota transitions. These deltas occasionally flip sign after downstream NetSuite normalization leading to negative or duplicate line items and manual interventions by billing ops.

Observed behavior and impact:
- Small population (~0.8% of monthly invoices) showing one or more invoice adjustments with amounts equal to ±1 or ±2 cents.
- Root cause chain: aggregator computes usage in floating point token units -> prorate/distribute discounts using fractional allocations -> exporter converts to decimal dollars with banker's rounding at export boundaries -> reconciliation uses per-interval bucketing that can reorder adjustments across hour boundaries when late usage is applied.
- Consequences: occasional negative Stripe line items, NetSuite export rejections, manual credits issued by support, and risk of mismatched accounting in downstream financial reports.

Goal:
- Make the billing export deterministic and elimination-prone for sub-cent/proration drift by normalizing to the smallest currency unit (cents for USD) at ledger level, applying deterministic tie-breaking and fixed-tiling for hourly buckets, and adding preventive sanity checks in the export pipeline.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Ledger canonicalization: round all intermediate allocations to integer smallest-currency-units (SCU) at the ledger commit point, rather than at export time. This means usage and discount allocations are represented in cents before any aggregation/rollup.
2) Deterministic tiling: when bucketing hourly usage for Stripe export, use a deterministic tiling algorithm that assigns fractional remainders to customer-consistent shards (hash(customer_id) % N) instead of relying on iteration order. This prevents reorder-induced sign flips caused by late-arriving deltas.
3) Export idempotency & checksum: compute a per-export checksum (ledger version + SCU totals + deterministic-tile-id) and persist it with export metadata. Exports with checksum mismatches go into a quarantine path rather than generating Stripe line items.
4) Backfill strategy: re-export only the invoices with checksum mismatches over the last 90 days. For any invoice where the canonical SCU total changes, create a single adjustment invoice item (positive or negative) and mark with metadata for audit.
5) Monitoring and alerts: add a metric for percent of invoices with non-zero SCU-adjustments after export, and an SLO to keep it < 0.05%. Alert escalates to billing-ops when breached.

Acceptance criteria:
- No Stripe invoice created by the new exporter path has fractional-dollar rounding (amounts must be integer SCUs).
- Deterministic tiling prevents reorder-induced sign flips in a synthetic replay test covering late-arriving usage and DST edge cases.
- Backfill produces at most one adjustment line per invoice and surfaces an audit ID to billing-ops.
- Dashboards show the new checksum metric and the percent-of-invoices-with-adjustment below 0.05% for 7 consecutive days in staging before prod rollout.

Engineering work breakdown:
- Backend (6 pts): implement SCU canonicalization at ledger commit, add deterministic-tiling function, add checksum generation, persist export metadata.
- Exporter (3 pts): modify Stripe/NetSuite exporters to read SCU totals and checksum; quarantine mismatches.
- Backfill tooling (3 pts): backfill runner to re-export last 90 days, idempotent adjustment creation.
- QA & E2E tests (2 pts): build synthetic replay harness (late usage, DST, multi-plan swap), and unit tests around rounding ties.
- Observability (1 pt): dashboards + alerting.

Migration & rollout plan:
1) Deploy SCU-canonicalization behind a feature flag in staging and run end-to-end synthetic replays against staging exporter.
2) Enable deterministic-tiling and checksum on staging exporter; verify quarantine path behavior and backfill dry-run.
3) Run backfill dry-run that computes adjustments but does not create Stripe items; verify results with billing-ops.
4) Gradually enable on production for low-volume accounts (alpha cohort) for 48 hours and monitor metrics.
5) Full rollout day: enable flag for all exports; run backfill for last 90 days in rolling batches with rate limits to avoid overload.

Rollback plan:
- Feature flags allow immediate revert to pre-change exporter behavior. If checksum quarantines spike >1% or negative-line items increase, flip the exporter flag and route quarantined exports to manual review.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Backfill may generate a large number of adjustment invoices during the first run. Mitigation: rate-limit backfill and aggregate adjustments into a single day for customers where possible; provide billing-ops with a preview report.
- Risk: SCU rounding could shift amounts for multi-currency customers (JPY vs USD). Mitigation: implement SCU per currency and add unit tests for each supported currency and precision.
- Risk: Deterministic tiling parameter N must be chosen to avoid hot-sharding. Mitigation: pick N=256 by default and validate distribution in prod telemetry.

Security & compliance:
- No PII changes. Export metadata includes ledger version and audit-id. Ensure audit logs are stored in customer FPM for compliance packages.

Next steps (short term):
- PR to implement SCU normalization prototype (assigned) and design review with accounting & billing-ops.
- Build replay harness and schedule staging validation for 2026-03-05.

Related notes and context:
- This ticket addresses a different failure mode than the "late-usage bucket overlap" incidents by eliminating rounding at export time and making bucket assignment deterministic.
- A previous export checksum experiment (see attachments) reduced drift but did not canonicalize SCU; this work builds on that experiment.
